structure.title: Fee Structure
items: Bill = base charge + usage (MJ) × unit price, plus 10% VAT
Residential gas has one price for cooking and heating and no seasonal price difference; winter bills are higher because usage rises
Unit price = nationwide wholesale rate (KOGAS) + retail supply cost set by each province/city
Meters read ㎥, bills use MJ: MJ = ㎥ × correction factor × heat value (about 42–43 MJ/㎥)

tips.title: Saving Tips
items: Lower the boiler setting by 1℃: about 7% less heating energy
For short trips out, lower the temperature by 2–3℃ instead of switching off
Seal window gaps with insulation tape and draft stoppers
Hot water is year-round base usage, so shorter showers save every month
Enter the MJ from your bill to project next month's cost

items.q: What's the difference between MJ and ㎥?
items.a: ㎥ is the volume on your meter; the bill is charged in MJ (energy). MJ = ㎥ × correction factor × heat value (about 42–43 MJ/㎥), so using the MJ on your bill is most accurate.
Yes. The wholesale rate (20.8495 KRW/MJ as of 2026-10-01) is nationwide, but the retail supply cost is set by each province/city. Seoul 22.5268, Gyeonggi 22.6226, Daegu 23.3459 KRW/MJ (excl. VAT).

items.q: How can I cut my winter gas bill?
items.a: Lowering the setting by 1℃ is commonly said to cut heating energy by about 7%. Check the savings section for your home's figure. For short trips out, lowering the temperature beats switching off.
